question: I used all my TFSA contribution room and then withdrew $2,000 during the current calendar year. Can I automatically contribute that $2,000 back immediately, and when does the withdrawal become new room?
generated_answer:
In Canada, the Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) program allows you to withdraw funds at any time, but the rules for re-contributing those funds can be a bit nuanced.

When you withdraw $2,000 from your TFSA during the current calendar year, you cannot immediately re-contribute that amount back into your TFSA in the same year, unless you have available contribution room.

The withdrawn amount of $2,000 will be added back to your TFSA contribution room at the beginning of the next calendar year. This is because the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) recalculates your TFSA contribution room on January 1st of each year.

Here's an example to illustrate this:

* You contribute the maximum amount to your TFSA and use up all your available contribution room.
* You withdraw $2,000 from your TFSA in, say, July of the current year.
* You cannot re-contribute the $2,000 back into your TFSA for the remainder of the current year, unless you have other available contribution room (e.g., from a previous year's unused room or from a TFSA contribution limit increase).
* On January 1st of the next calendar year, the $2,000 you withdrew will be added back to your TFSA contribution room, allowing you to re-contribute that amount, in addition to any other available contribution room for that year.

It's essential to keep track of your TFSA contributions and withdrawals to avoid over-contributing, which can result in penalties and interest charges from the CRA. If you're unsure about your TFSA contribution room or have questions about re-contributing withdrawn funds, consider consulting with a financial advisor or contacting the CRA directly for guidance.
